invariants: A decimal is place value continued past the ones: computing in the smallest shared place turns g5dc add ragged into whole-number arithmetic, and the point's position records which place the digits landed in.
misconceptions: Right-aligning digits instead of the points, treating a trailing zero as a change in value, or losing count of the decimal places a product carries.

widget.prompt: What does the zero in 5.20 contribute to the value?

options.label: It adds no value.
options.feedback: Correct — a trailing zero fills a place but adds no value.

options.label: It adds one hundredth.
options.feedback: The zero SITS in the hundredths place, but a zero digit counts zero hundredths — 5.20 holds not one hundredth more than 5.2.

options.label: It adds one tenth.
options.feedback: The tenths place already holds the 2, and the zero sits one place further right — and a zero digit adds no amount in any place.

options.label: It rounds the number.
options.feedback: Nothing is rounded — 5.20 and 5.2 name exactly the same amount; the zero only gives the hundredths column a digit to work with.

widget.prompt: To add 4.6 + 2.83 in columns, a classmate refuses to write 4.6 as 4.60, saying the extra zero would change the total. Which reply is right?

options.label: The zero changes nothing — it only gives the hundredths column a digit
options.feedback: Correct — 4.60 names the same amount as 4.6, and now the 3 of 2.83 has a hundredths digit to line up with.

options.label: The classmate is right — 4.60 is one hundredth more than 4.6
options.feedback: The zero digit counts zero hundredths, so 4.60 and 4.6 name exactly the same amount.

options.label: Padding is only allowed when subtracting, never when adding
options.feedback: Padding renames a number without changing it, so any column work — adding or subtracting — may use it.

options.label: Skip padding and add the 3 of 2.83 to the 6 of 4.6 instead
options.feedback: The 6 counts tenths and the 3 counts hundredths — adding digits from different places mixes piece sizes, which is exactly what padding prevents.
